messages.author: 9783d9fe56013431
messages.subject: sliding window analysis
parts:
Is there a way within Plyr to perform a moving average where the user
has control over step size and window size? Something similar to filter
() but filter has no apparent control over step size and also has no
apparent tracking of other variables in the dataset.

For example, say I have a dataset with Position, Variable, Value
Position starts at 1 and goes to 100,000 stepping 1 each row. I want
to average over 100 Values (for any give variable) and then choose the
step size to take before calculating the next average. Non-overlapping
windows would result in 1000 values (first one from position 1:100,
second from position 101:200, etc). I'd like the output to contain the
range of Positions covered as well as the average value. Overlapping
windows might step by 10, but still average over 100, so would result
in the second entry covering position 11:110.

It seems like dlply could do this but I'm not sure how. I'm not at the
level of writing functions within R so really am looking for something
already built but which has flexibility for choosing step size and
window size.

Many thanks,
squid.

my head. Maybe someone else on the mailing list will have some ideas.

Hadley

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: sliding window analysis
parts:
And this was the trick I was thinking off for making rolling indicies:

roll <- function(n, size) {
stopifnot(n > size)
outer(1:(n - size + 1), 0:(size - 1), "+")
}

Hadley
